explanations: C-1. Compared with no Halvern Steel Safeguard Order, price paid for buyers.construction rises from the medium run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: TX-7: a tariff the foreign sellers do not absorb raises what domestic buyers pay and lets protected domestic producers charge and sell more; RS-14: a dearer input is passed down to the output: its price rises where competitors face the same cost, and its sellers sell less where competitors are exempt. This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72); The taxed good is a material part of downstream costs and cannot be replaced at the old cost (p = 0.65). Reported.

C-2. Compared with no Halvern Steel Safeguard Order, quantity supplied for export_industries falls from the medium run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: TX-7: a tariff the foreign sellers do not absorb raises what domestic buyers pay and lets protected domestic producers charge and sell more; TX-2: a tax on each unit opens a wedge between what buyers pay and what sellers keep, and the market shrinks; TX-8: foreigners who sell less to the country earn less of its currency and so buy fewer of its exports. This holds if: Imports remain a meaningful share of supply, and foreign sellers do not absorb most of the tariff (p = 0.72); The fall in imports is not offset by capital flows or other adjustments within the medium run (p = 0.35). Not reported: an assumption is below the 0.5 cut-off.

evidence: Three domestic steel firms supply about 60% of the steel used in Halvern; the rest is imported (WE-013 record).
Halvern buys a small share of the world's steel and has a floating exchange rate (WE-013 record).
answer.rationale: Imports are about 40% of supply and Halvern buys a small share of world steel, so foreign sellers have little reason to absorb most of the tariff and imports should stay a meaningful share.

question.text: Do imports remain a meaningful share of supply after the tariff, and will foreign sellers fail to absorb most of it (they have many other markets, the country buys a small share of the world's supply)?

evidence: Three domestic steel firms supply about 60% of the steel used in Halvern; the rest is imported (WE-013 record).
The standard for "sufficient quantity or quality" is not defined.
answer.rationale: Domestic firms supply about 60% of steel and the exclusion process presumes some products are not produced domestically in sufficient quantity or quality, so close substitutes for most imports are unlikely in the medium run.

question.text: Can domestic producers raise output (spare or idle capacity) and make close substitutes for most imports?

evidence: Halvern is a mid-sized trading country with its own currency and a floating exchange rate.
answer.rationale: The floating exchange rate is the kind of adjustment channel that tends to offset part of a tariff-driven fall in imports, so the fall is more likely offset than left unoffset.

question.text: Is the fall in imports left unoffset by capital flows or other adjustments in the currency market within the medium run?

evidence: About 4,000 domestic manufacturers use steel as a main input (WE-013 record).
answer.rationale: Steel is a main input for about 4,000 domestic manufacturers, and the record gives no sign of cheap medium-run replacement, so the taxed input is likely hard to replace at the old cost.

question.text: Is the taxed good a material part of the downstream users' costs, and can they not replace it at the old cost in the medium run (other materials, other designs)?

evidence: Imported fabricated steel products and finished goods containing steel (machinery, vehicles, appliances, fabricated structural sections, fasteners) are not covered.
answer.rationale: Imported finished goods containing steel (machinery, vehicles, appliances) are not covered, so steel-using downstream makers compete with sellers who do not face the 25% tariff.

question.text: Do the downstream users compete with sellers who do not face the higher cost (imported finished goods, untaxed products)?

components.cap_unit: ad valorem, share of customs value, for three years
source_sentences: Importers of record must pay a tariff of 25% of the customs value on imports of flat-rolled and long steel products, for three years.
Imported fabricated steel products and finished goods containing steel (machinery, vehicles, appliances, fabricated structural sections, fasteners) are not covered.
